summary: Compact lower-semicontinuous finite convex costs genuinely yield optimizers and the claimed scalar value properties. Arbitrary maximizing selections recover the full shared network and its signed biased affine output. Hard and entropy specializations use actual formulas.

model_correspondence.evidence: Regularizer contains only a finite real cost, lower semicontinuity, convexity and nonpositivity on actual Icc 0 1. Compactness and upper semicontinuity construct the optimizer. Its objective maximum is proved an IsGreatest and actual supremum, not assumed.

model_correspondence.topic: Convex value, monotonicity, Lipschitz bound, derivative
model_correspondence.evidence: Each maximizing probability supplies an affine lower support. Actual probability interval bounds yield monotonicity and 1-Lipschitz continuity. Fermat gives every optimizer equals deriv only at differentiable points; nonunique hard ties are not silently declared differentiable.

pairWith subtracts cost in its positive stream; validity follows optimizer value equality, and nonnegativity follows nonpositive cost. Network.forwardWith and decomposeWith use the same arbitrary varying-width network and actual biases. The ungated final affine readout includes unrestricted signed weight difference and signed bias difference.

Zero cost hardGate explicitly stops at zero and yields literal stopPair. Actual negative binary entropy has sigmoid optimizer against every probability including endpoints, value softplus, and literal softSplit pair. An independent consumer derives arbitrary chosen entropy gate equals sigmoid from generic derivative uniqueness.

boundary_cases: shifted constant nonpositive cost gives ReLU+2 without endpoint normalization
hard tie has both optimizers but distinct streams
canonical gate makes arbitrary-selection hypothesis satisfiable
any selected entropy optimizer equals sigmoid
signed affine readout with negative output and bias

scope_limits: Finite real costs on the closed probability interval, matching the stated source codomain; extended-real barrier costs are not claimed.
No generic smoothness, second-derivative absolute continuity, or GeLU/Swish representation follows from this theorem.
The maximizing selection can alter the two streams at nondifferentiable ties; the reconstructed difference is selection independent.
